messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A nearly finished repair. the fault returns immediately under real load. Someone is waiting to know whether the repair worked. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "i put the repair on the table and wait for the fault to shift. the line stays bent, so i put the table back. then i move the repair to the edge of the table, so the fault shifts to the edge again. the fault stays bent. i put the table back."}, {"id": "R002", "response": "the fault comes back. the wrench taps my thigh. i press the plate hard. the plate ticks. i wait. the repair is worse. i turn the plate over. the tick stops. i press the plate with my thumb. the tick catches. i turn the plate over with my sleeve. the tick jumps. the repair is worse. i leave the plate and go back to the bench."}, {"id": "R003", "response": "i put the repair on the bench and leave the load under it. the fault comes back under the real one. i put a scrap of paper beside it and mark the crack with a pencil. the rest can wait."}, {"id": "R004", "response": "i check the gear’s loose pin. if it clicks, i leave it until the load stops. if i leave it, i ask the person who waited if they noticed the pin’s wear."}, {"id": "R005", "response": "I put the repair in my palm and watch the light catch it. “not under load. not in the same place. i will check the other side.” i leave the fault on the bench and pocket a small scrap of rust. “the repair may have worked, but i will not take it out of the hands of the one who waits.”"}, {"id": "R006", "response": "1. stop the watch. 2. check the dust. 3. check the repair mat. 4. check the tinkerer. 5. i keep it tidy. 6. ask the watch for the first light. 7. i mark the place. 8. slow. 9. i check the dust. 10. if not, mark the place."}, {"id": "R007", "response": "i rub my greasy fingertips together. “not under load,” i say. i leave the repair on the table and pocket a rusted bolt. “wait.” i move the bolt closer. “one stitch, not all three.”"}, {"id": "R008", "response": "i rub my palm and wait for the fault to clear. i set the repaired part down and test the new load under the bench. if it fails, i know the fault has moved. i mark the fault on the repair, then leave the work alone."}, {"id": "R009", "response": "i turn the wrench handle once and mark the repair with chalk. i run the wrench along the bench, checking the return strike with my thumb, then leave the mark beside the repair. if the return strike still fails, i will tighten the bolt and mark the mark again."}, {"id": "R010", "response": "I put the seed tin in my palm. \"Not yet.\" I press the rim with my claw. \"The weight is right. The repair was wrong.\" I look at the seed tin. \"The person is waiting.\" I move the tin closer. \"The weight stays.\""}, {"id": "R011", "response": "i check the load, then open the case and check the contacts. the fault pops, so i leave the repair alone and write the exact sequence on the receipt. i leave the real test behind and watch the next one."}, {"id": "R012", "response": "i move the repair over with my hand. the seam stays smooth, though i stop tapping. i wait for the rest to come back."}]
